entities.name: Small Sieve
entities.evidence: Small Sieve is a simple – possibly disposable – Python backdoor which is distributed using an NSIS installer

entities.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python
entities.evidence: Small Sieve is a PyInstaller-packed Python script

entities.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
entities.evidence: Small Sieve is started by a registry run key

entities.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
entities.evidence: Small Sieve uses a custom hex byte swapping encoding scheme combined with an obfuscated base64 function to protect program strings

entities.name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
entities.evidence: Small Sieve uses variations of Microsoft (Microsift) and Outlook in its filenames to attempt to avoid detection

entities.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
entities.evidence: Small Sieve beacons and tasking are performed using the Telegram API over HTTPS

entities.name: Data Encoding: Non-Standard Encoding
entities.evidence: Small Sieve employs a custom hex byte swapping encoding scheme to obfuscate tasking traffic

entities.name: Execution Guardrails
entities.evidence: The Small Sieve payload will only execute correctly if the word 'Platypus' is passed to it on the command line

entities.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
entities.evidence: The url will be fetched and saved to the provided filename using the Python urllib module urlretrieve function

entities.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
entities.evidence: Any commands other than those detailed in Table 2 are executed directly by passing them to `cmd.exe /c`
